dimension: Information architecture and troubleshooting (benchmark section 5 first half; priorities 1 and 3)

Use hub (/use/) is ordered Install it -> Open it and work -> image software (guides/install/, guides/using-apps/, guides/image-software/) and has a visible 'Something went wrong?' line linking to Troubleshooting an installed app (data/hubs.yaml use.help). Use-track previous/next follows task order (read from the pager of each built page): install -> using-apps -> notebook-usage -> troubleshooting-installed-app -> image-software -> napari -> fiji -> qupath.

install.md (template, shown as /guides/install/) has OS headings Windows / macOS / Linux, the 'Windows protected your PC' > 'More info' > 'Run anyway' picture, the macOS 'Open Anyway' path and an Intel-vs-Apple-Silicon chooser. Verified in the search UI: 'Windows protected your PC' -> install/#windows (1 result), 'Open Anyway' -> install/#macos, 'Apple Silicon or Intel' -> app pages' 'Get it' and install/#macos.

Search reaches an actionable page for: 'JupyterLab does not start' -> troubleshooting-installed-app (only result), 'certificate error', 'uninstall', 'requirements.yaml' -> notebook-requirements (top 3), 'workflow failed' -> troubleshooting repository setup + workflow-status, 'manifest' / 'labconstrictor-app.yaml' -> app-manifest and submit, 'use inside Fiji' -> image-software (top) then the Fiji/ecosystem entries, 'app won't open' -> using-apps#something-went-wrong.

using-apps.md ('Something went wrong' section) links install, troubleshooting-installed-app and the app's 'Report a problem'; each host guide (napari, fiji, qupath) has an 'If something does not work' section with doctor, Details... and the log path; executable_creation.md ends with '3. After the release' (try the installer yourself, then list the app).

app-manifest.md gives the real labconstrictor-app.yaml example with comments on each field and the editor-validation schema URL; notebook_requirements.md shows the three required requirements.yaml fields. The raw facts for a reference exist, they are just not in a Reference area (see gap 6).

gaps.requirement: Troubleshooting organised by visible symptoms and error messages, no jargon (TLS, environments, manifests) before the reader finds help; search should understand problems (priority 3; section 5 'Troubleshooting' row)
gaps.current: The only user-facing page, troubleshooting_installed_app.md (built at /guides/troubleshooting-installed-app/), has two entries. Entry 2 is titled 'JupyterLab does not start because Windows reports an ASN.1 certificate error': the heading states the cause, not what the person sees; the body opens with 'LabConstrictor-based installers include a TLS-resilient launcher... before JupyterLab imports Tornado... CA-bundle fallback', then 'pip-system-certs', 'constructor environment', 'PEM', env variables like MY_PROJECT_CA_BUNDLE, and 'Maintainers can run ... launch_jupyter.py --self-test'. No quoted error text and no steps a biologist can perform. Entry 1 (Windows still lists the app after uninstalling) links to 'the uninstalling guide' = download_executable.md, whose whole content on origin/main is 'Sorry, but no executable files are available yet' - there is no uninstall instruction anywhere on the site. Symptoms that are only mentioned in install.md or not at all: macOS refuses the .pkg, app opens no browser tab, terminal window closed by mistake (only a note in notebook_usage.md section 2), Linux .sh not running. Zero search results (verified in the site's search UI) for 'Mac cannot open app', 'macOS blocked', 'macOS says damaged', 'blocked by Windows', 'installer blocked', 'browser did not open', 'SmartScreen', 'unidentified developer'.
gaps.proposal: Template repo, .tools/docs/troubleshooting_installed_app.md (the site imports it; do not copy it): rewrite as symptom headings in the reader's words, each with what you see, why in one sentence, and numbered fix steps, e.g. 'Windows says "Windows protected your PC"', 'macOS says the installer cannot be opened', 'The browser does not open after I start the app', 'I closed the black terminal window', 'The app is still listed after I uninstalled it', 'JupyterLab does not start (certificate error on Windows)'. Quote the exact message strings. Move the TLS/CA-bundle/self-test text into one 'For maintainers and IT administrators' section at the bottom, with jargon explained or collapsed. Add the missing uninstall steps (Windows, macOS, Linux) to this page or install.md and repoint the broken 'uninstalling guide' link. Use the symptom words (Mac, blocked, cannot open, damaged, protected) in headings so the client-side search finds them. Site side: nothing to change; the page title in data/hubs.yaml use.help can stay.
gaps.rule_conflicts: none (AGENTS.md: template repo is the source of truth for this page; 'Menu titles are the page's first heading' so renaming the h1 renames the menu entry; if a section is renamed, anchors used by other pages must be kept or the site check_site anchors check will fail).

gaps.requirement: A visitor arriving from an app's download tiles lands on installation instructions for their OS, not the docs home (section 5, last paragraph)
gaps.current: On /apps/nucleisky/ the download buttons go straight to the GitHub release asset (target=_blank). The only links to the install guide are (a) 'Need help installing? See the install guide.' -> ../../guides/install/ (pages_apps.py:100) and (b) the section 'How to install' (id=install) -> ../../guides/install/. Neither carries an anchor, although the built install page has per-OS anchors (#windows, #macos, #linux: the search UI returns install/#windows and install/#macos). The tile's own hint line is plain text (pages_apps.os_tile, lines 66-68: 'If Windows warns you, choose More info, then Run anyway.', 'Not sure? Apple menu, About This Mac...', 'Run it with: bash <file name>') with no link, so a Mac user who has downloaded the .pkg and gets the Gatekeeper message has no link to the 'Open Anyway' steps from the tile. lc.js (lcInitSystem) highlights the visitor's tile but adds no link. I did not find any page that opens the install guide at the visitor's own OS.
gaps.proposal: Site repo, scripts/lcsite/pages_apps.py: in os_tile add a link to the hint line, 'Step by step for Windows' -> ../../guides/install/#windows (and #macos, #linux), using non-generic link text (check_design.py rule). Point the 'Need help installing?' sentence at install/ too, but let the per-tile link be the main route. Optionally in lc.js lcInitSystem rewrite the generic install links to the visitor's #os anchor. check_site.py already fails on dead anchors, which guards the ids if the template ever renames the headings. Add a test beside the existing os_tile tests.

The anchors depend on the template headings 'Windows', 'macOS', 'Linux' in install.md (source of truth stays in the template).

None has a heading or sentence for the commonest first-run failure: the widget/menu opens but the app is not listed, or the menu entry is missing after installing the plugin. The parent guide image-software.md (headings: 'Three steps', 'Check that everything works', 'Make your own tools') has no troubleshooting section at all and its step 1 only says the installer 'registers the app'. Verified in search UI: 'app not showing in napari' and 'napari plugin not showing' return no result; 'doctor' returns the three generic sections. The real messages exist in the Tools repo but are not reachable: docs/OPERATIONS.md lines 29-37 (Troubleshooting), HUMAN_TEST_PROTOCOL.md:134 'WARNING: tool registration failed', 'skipped: CellTracksColab: not available on this machine (interpreter ... is missing)'. This site does not fetch OPERATIONS.md.

gaps.requirement: A Reference area: manifest fields, requirements.yaml format, release naming, supported integrations (section 5 Reference row)
gaps.current: No Reference group exists in guide_nav (groups are Install and open / Use apps in your image software / From zero to installed notebooks / Notebook authoring tips / Examples / GitHub management) or in the top menu (Home, Apps, Docs, Ecosystem, Submit your app). Facts are scattered inside how-tos: manifest fields = one commented example in app-manifest.md plus 'More optional fields exist (authors, DOI, license, screenshots, a quick start); the full list is in the schema', which links to a JSON schema file (schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json), not a readable page; requirements.yaml = Option 2, step 1 of notebook_requirements.md (dependencies, python_version, description); release naming = one IMPORTANT note about semantic versioning in executable_creation.md and the installer file name pattern (MyApp-0.1.0-Linux-x86_64.sh) only appears as an example in install.md; supported integrations = image-software.md and the napari/Fiji/QuPath guides, plus data/hosts.yaml. Search 'release name' returns submit and workflow-status, not a reference.
gaps.proposal: Smallest step, without a new top-level section: add one 'Reference' group at the end of the sidebar with 2 pages. (a) Site repo: a generated 'App manifest fields' page produced at build time from schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json (a table: field, required, type, allowed values, description), in a new module scripts/lcsite/reference.py (functions <= 30 lines, tests), so nothing is written twice; app-manifest.md then links to it instead of the raw JSON. (b) Template repo: a short .tools/docs/reference.md (requirements.yaml fields with a full example, tag format X.Y.Z, installer file name pattern per OS and architecture, where the files appear), listed in the README group 'Reference'. Supported integrations: link the existing image-software guide from that group instead of duplicating it. Do not build API docs.
